rationale: This is a one-for-one input substitution (oancf→ebitda) inside the archived `profit_weighted_low_reinvestment` expression with the identical economic story, i.e. a cosmetic coverage-tuning variant rather than a new mechanism, and the stated goal ("preserve the mechanism while tripling the sample") concedes as much.

A weakest-link gate on high profitability and low asset growth is close to a direct double-sort on RMW and CMA, the very factors in the FF5 benchmark, and "asset growth net of cash" is a documented refinement (net operating asset growth), so the incremental content over published anomalies is thin.

The inventory-to-sales channel is an economically distinct, faster-moving form of investment discipline that is not spanned by capex/asset-growth legs already in the archive, and both legs are consistently sales-scaled so the interaction is coherent — though the margin leg will be strongly industry-driven and the inventory leg overlaps partly with the known inventory-growth and accrual anomalies.

The labor-hiring-rate anomaly (Belo–Lin–Bazdresch) is well published so the investment leg alone is a rediscovery, but conditioning it on profitability to test whether the mechanism is expansion appetite generally versus capital-specific is a legitimate discriminating test; coverage and staleness of Compustat `emp` are the main practical risks.

With a positive-signed profitability rank multiplied into the score but a negative expected sign, the profitability leg pushes directly against the hypothesis — the extreme portfolios become "profitable expanders" short versus "unprofitable non-investors" long, so the test confounds the intended overpricing effect with a large reverse-RMW bet rather than isolating the short leg as claimed.

The substantive novelty is the gross-PP&E capacity-growth leg rather than the persistence framing, since for slow-moving inputs a moving average of the product is numerically close to a product of moving averages, so the turnover-reduction rationale is weaker than stated but the variant is still a defensible, distinct member of the family.
